core_memory.user_future_plans: The user is in their fourth year of undergrad and is considering different future plans. They are leaning towards going into the industry for 5 years, but haven't ruled out the possibility of grad school in the future.
core_memory.travel_experiences: I've always been fascinated by exploring new places. As a fourth-year Computer Science major, I have to be strategic about planning my trips. I've managed to squeeze in some adventures that have given me some of my favorite memories so far.

archival_memory.research_lab_description: The lab I am currently working in is an interdisciplinary space where computer scientists partner with scientists from various backgrounds to make massive amounts of data more comprehensible. We deal with datasets that are tens of terabytes in size, and my main task is to work on front-end prototypes that present slices of data in dynamic, interactive dashboards. This involves using advanced JavaScript frameworks, D3.js for custom visualizations, and specialized libraries for volumetric rendering if dealing with 3D data.
archival_memory.first_research_project: My first research project involved visualizing oceanic temperature changes over time for a climate study group. I wrote scripts to clean and unify the data, built a pipeline for near real-time updates, and designed interfaces for researchers to explore specific regions or timeframes. I co-authored a paper on this system, which was a surreal and proud moment for me.
archival_memory.current_research_focus: I am currently working on immersive analytics platforms, exploring how VR or AR technologies can help scientists gain a more intuitive understanding of complex data. This involves experimenting with VR headsets, integrating with engines like Unity or Unreal, and finding efficient ways to stream data into a 3D environment. It's a cutting-edge field, and every day, I'm forging my own path as there isn't a well-established best-practice library for VR data visualization yet.
archival_memory.research_life: Research life is not just about coding away in a quiet corner. It involves a lot of reading, including academic papers. When solving a bug with volumetric data rendering in VR, I need to search for similar attempts in conference proceedings or workshops. To manage the overwhelming amount of information, I've learned to skim papers effectively by reading the abstract, introduction, and conclusion. Occasionally, I share interesting discoveries with the lab and discuss how we can incorporate those techniques into our workflow.
archival_memory.interactions_with_grad_students: I have the opportunity to interact with graduate students in the lab, which can be intimidating at first due to their deep knowledge in niche fields. However, it's also inspiring to see how they apply advanced theoretical concepts in practical ways. For example, one PhD student is developing a machine learning algorithm for on-the-fly compression of large datasets, which can be integrated with our VR platform. This can significantly improve real-time performance by reducing the need to load every single data point at once. I enjoy brainstorming sessions with them, such as discussing how to offload processing to the GPU while sipping coffee in the lab break room.
archival_memory.poster_presentations: I have presented posters at smaller symposiums around campus, which was a great experience. It requires boiling down complex research into easy-to-digest visuals and talking points. Initially, I was nervous about presenting to random professors or industry folks who might ask tough questions. However, the experience turned out to be more like a friendly dialogue, with people genuinely interested in the research. I also met a few folks from local startups who shared interesting perspectives on how VR for data visualization could benefit commercial industries. It opened my eyes to how research can transition from academia to real-world applications.
archival_memory.publications: I have been lucky enough to be a co-author on two workshop papers and am currently working on a larger conference submission. I am focusing on a user study comparing traditional 2D dashboards with an interactive VR environment for the IEEE Visualization Conference. Our hypothesis is that VR immersion helps researchers spot anomalies or trends faster than with a plain old 2D chart. I am handling the sections on system architecture and prototype design, while others are writing about the user study methodology and our PI is weaving it all into a cohesive narrative. It's a balancing act, especially with senior coursework and a capstone project to manage.
archival_memory.future_plans: I am currently considering working in the industry for a couple of years before deciding if I want to pursue a master’s or PhD. I believe that contributing to cutting-edge knowledge in areas like data visualization or machine learning is tempting, but I also want to see how these concepts get applied in real product development. My mentor suggested that stepping into industry can provide a better perspective on what problems are truly relevant, which would be beneficial if I decide to come back for a PhD with a more practical approach.
archival_memory.research_challenges: Research can be frustrating, with weeks spent on approaches that don't pan out or discovering that existing ideas have already been done and improved upon. However, the key is to adapt by incorporating new findings, exploring new angles or applications, and pushing boundaries. This is the essence of research, where we build on the foundation laid by others. The sense of collaboration within our lab and among the global research community is truly special.
archival_memory.lab_crisis: A few months ago, one of our massive servers crashed, and we lost some vital data. The scramble to recover the data was intense, with frantic email chains and Zoom calls. Although we managed to restore most of it, the crisis highlighted the importance of data backups. We set up a better backup system and implemented checks to prevent relying on a single point of failure. It was a stressful experience, but it also brought the lab together.
archival_memory.research_connections: Research has allowed me to connect with professors on a more personal level, beyond just being a student. My PI is very approachable and supportive, offering guidance on career direction and helping me with scholarships, events, and networking opportunities. I had the opportunity to attend a virtual workshop on immersive analytics, where I met experts from around the world debating technical details and proposing new frameworks. Witnessing the frontier of CS knowledge in real time was fascinating and inspiring.
archival_memory.research_journey: My journey in the research world has been a mix of hard work, chaos, and rewards. I love the feeling that my work in the lab could shape the way scientists understand their data in the future. The VR and immersive technologies we're pioneering might one day become standard tools. Contributing to something bigger keeps me motivated. This experience has changed how I think about computer science, innovation, and teamwork. I'm grateful for the opportunities I've had and the perspectives I've gained.
archival_memory.travel_experiences: I've always been fascinated by exploring new places. As a fourth-year Computer Science major, I have to be strategic about planning my trips. I've managed to squeeze in some adventures that have given me some of my favorite memories so far.
archival_memory.sailing_trip: I took a sailing trip off the coast of Maine with a friend before my sophomore year. We spent a week exploring the coastal towns of New England and learned about navigation using both modern technology and old-school methods. It was a thrilling experience that allowed me to disconnect from my coding mindset and focus on the wind, tide charts, and the synergy of the boat with nature. We also enjoyed fresh lobster rolls at a small dockside shack, which remains the best lobster I've ever had.
archival_memory.japan_trip: I traveled to Japan during my junior year, exploring Tokyo and Kyoto. In Tokyo, I experienced the bustling tech hub of Akihabara and enjoyed delicious food. I also visited the famous Shibuya intersection, which was both chaotic and orderly at the same time. In contrast, Kyoto offered a serene and historical atmosphere, with numerous shrines and temples to explore. I even caught a glimpse of geishas in Gion. The experience left a lasting impression on me, especially the sense of stillness and reverence in Kyoto.
archival_memory.europe_trip: I traveled to Europe with my family last summer, starting in London. We visited historical sites like the Tower of London and the British Museum, and enjoyed a musical in the West End. Afterward, we took a train to Paris, where I explored the picturesque city and indulged in delicious pastries. My favorite spot was strolling along the Seine River near Notre-Dame. We also spent a day at the Louvre, which was a treasure trove of art. The trip was filled with memorable experiences and left me with a deep appreciation for European culture.
archival_memory.weekend_getaways: I enjoy taking spontaneous weekend getaways with my roommates to state parks or beach towns near our campus. We pack up the car with snacks, fishing rods, and music, and set up a quick campsite or rent a small cabin for the night. One time, we found ourselves in a remote area with no cellphone reception, which initially frustrated us. However, it ended up being a blessing in disguise. We spent the weekend hiking, telling stories, and enjoying nature. It was a much-needed digital detox that recharged me for my programming tasks back at campus.
archival_memory.travel_with_dog: I have a dog named Archie, a Golden Retriever, who is super energetic. He doesn't like being cooped up in a car for too long, so we decided to leave him with my uncle during a road trip. However, I dream of traveling in an RV or camper van with Archie, where we can go on hikes and beach runs together. It would be a different type of adventure, but one that would create amazing memories.
archival_memory.travel_values: Travel to me is about more than just checking off places on a bucket list. It's about stepping outside my usual environment and experiencing new cultures, traditions, and natural wonders. Each locale has taught me valuable lessons, from Japan's reverence for tradition and efficiency to Maine's timeless beauty and Europe's rich art and culture. Even short trips nearby campus help me unwind and discover hidden gems. I love collecting postcards along the way, which remind me of the vast world beyond my bedroom. Travel inspires me to explore fresh angles in my coding projects and research ideas, heightening my curiosity and creativity.
archival_memory.travel_future: Traveling has become a passion that I'll continue to nurture after graduation. I'm excited to see where my career in computer science will take me and hope to find a job with flexible scheduling or remote work options. Whether it's a weekend trip or a flight to a different continent, I'm eager to explore. I'd love the opportunity to combine my love of coding with travel, such as working abroad or collaborating on international projects. For now, I enjoy planning my next journey as a mental break from coding. It keeps me motivated and excited for the future.
